newsitem.title: CANADA: NBA BASKETBALL-WILLIAMS LEADS WAY AS CELTICS SCORE RARE ROAD WIN.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-WILLIAMS LEADS WAY AS CELTICS SCORE RARE ROAD WIN.

text.p: Eric Williams scored six of his season-high 27 points in a pivotal 15-0 third-quarter run as the Boston Celtics recorded a rare road win with a 114-102 victory over the Toronto Raptors on Monday.
Todd Day scored 26 points and David Wesley added 25, 11 assists and seven rebounds for the Celtics, who won away from home for just the second time in 19 road games this season.
"It was a nice way to bounce back from yesterday's loss to Vancouver," Boston coach M.L. Carr said of Sunday's 102-92 home loss.

"It was great team effort, a good distribution of scoring. Our guys need some small victories since this team has struggled," added Carr, whose club ended a 15-game losing streak against Eastern Conference foes.
Damon Stoudamire had 26 points and 10 assists and Popeye Jones added 18 for the Raptors.
Toronto led 74-65 with 6:47 left in the third quarter before Boston began its key 15-0 run to take control.

Marcus Camby pulled Toronto within 91-85 with 9:47 remaining. But Antoine Walker, who finished with 20 points and 13 rebounds, made a pair of layups to extend the lead to 10 points and Boston pulled away down the stretch.
In San Antonio, Mitch Richmond scored 26 points and combined with Jeff Grayer for 11 points in an 20-0 second-half run as the Sacramento Kings beat the Spurs 85-79.
Grayer finished with 16 points and Olden Polynice had 15 and 17 rebounds for the Kings, who snapped a seven-game losing streak at San Antonio, going back to April, 1993.
Vernon Maxwell scored 15 points and Dominique Wilkins added 13 for the Spurs, who were held below 80 points for the 12th time this season.
The Spurs were outscored 46-30 in the second half.
At Utah, Karl Malone scored 14 of his 24 points in the first half as the Jazz used a 16-0 first-half run to pull away for a 111-89 pounding of the Washington Bullets.
Stephen Howard scored 16 points and Bryon Russell added 15 for Utah, which won for the sixth time in seven games.
The Jazz have yet to lose at the Delta Centre in 1997, reeling off nine consecutive home wins.
Gheorghe Muresan scored 18 points and Rod Strickland and Tracy Murray had 11 apiece for the Bullets, who have dropped the first three games of their four-game West Coast trip.
